factFindings.finding: Verified Preparatory phase fact against PDF page image(s) 7: Consumes 2 ATP and produces 2 glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate molecules per glucose.
Verified Payoff phase fact against PDF page image(s) 8, 25: Forms 4 ATP and 2 NADH per glucose; after the investment, net ATP gain is 2.
Verified Net carbon balance fact against PDF page image(s) 6: One glucose becomes 2 pyruvate molecules through 10 enzyme-catalyzed reactions.
Verified Retention fact against PDF page image(s) 10: Phosphate groups prevent glycolytic intermediates from leaving the cell.
Verified Catalysis and energy fact against PDF page image(s) 10: They contribute to energy conservation, lower activation energy and increase enzyme specificity.
Verified Hexokinase fact against PDF page image(s) 12: Glucose is phosphorylated at C6 using ATP; Mg2+ is required and the step is intracellularly irreversible.
Verified PFK-1 fact against PDF page image(s) 16: ATP phosphorylates fructose 6-phosphate to fructose 1,6-bisphosphate; this is the first committed step.
Verified Aldolase fact against PDF page image(s) 17: Cleaves fructose 1,6-bisphosphate into glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate (aldose) and DHAP (ketose).
Verified Triose phosphate isomerase fact against PDF page image(s) 18: Reversibly converts DHAP to glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate, finishing the preparatory phase.
Verified Phosphoglycerate kinase fact against PDF page image(s) 21: 1,3-Bisphosphoglycerate donates phosphate to ADP, producing 3-phosphoglycerate and ATP.
Verified Pyruvate kinase fact against PDF page image(s) 24: PEP donates phosphate to ADP, producing pyruvate and ATP; K+ and Mg2+ or Mn2+ are required.
Verified Glycolytic oxidation fact against PDF page image(s) 20: Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate + Pi + NAD+ forms 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate, NADH and H+.
Verified Lactate fact against PDF page image(s) 28: Pyruvate reduction to lactate consumes NADH and regenerates NAD+.
Verified Ethanol fact against PDF page image(s) 30: Pyruvate→acetaldehyde releases CO2; acetaldehyde reduction to ethanol regenerates NAD+.
Verified Pyruvate decarboxylase fact against PDF page image(s) 30: Uses Mg2+ and TPP to form acetaldehyde; humans lack this enzyme.
Verified Alcohol dehydrogenase fact against PDF page image(s) 30: Uses Zn2+ and NADH to reduce acetaldehyde to ethanol.
Verified Muscle fact against PDF page image(s) 33: Anaerobic glycolysis forms lactate and gains 2 ATP in the illustrated cycle.

Verified Liver fact against PDF page image(s) 29, 33: Lactate arrives in blood and is converted to glucose; the diagram indicates 6 ATP used. Six ATP is retained as the supplied diagram label in reference text, not scored as a literal ATP/GTP distinction.
Verified Pyruvate carboxylase fact against PDF page image(s) 37: Pyruvate + bicarbonate + ATP forms oxaloacetate; biotin is required and acetyl-CoA activates.
Verified PEP carboxykinase fact against PDF page image(s) 40: Converts oxaloacetate to PEP with CO2 release.
Verified Actual conditions fact against PDF page image(s) 40: Overall standard free energy is +0.9 kJ/mol, while stated actual free energy is −25 kJ/mol.
Verified Attachment fact against PDF page image(s) 38: An amide bond links biotin to the ε-amino group of an enzyme lysine.
Verified Transfer fact against PDF page image(s) 38: ATP activates bicarbonate, biotin is carboxylated, then carries CO2 to the second site where pyruvate becomes oxaloacetate.
Verified Malate route fact against PDF page image(s) 39: Mitochondrial oxaloacetate is reduced using NADH; exported malate is reoxidized in cytosol, forming NADH.
Verified Lactate precursor fact against PDF page image(s) 41: Lactate oxidation to pyruvate already produces cytosolic NADH, reducing the need to export malate.
Verified FBPase-1 fact against PDF page image(s) 42: Hydrolyzes fructose 1,6-bisphosphate C1 phosphate to yield fructose 6-phosphate and Pi.
Verified Glucose 6-phosphatase fact against PDF page image(s) 43: Hydrolyzes glucose 6-phosphate to glucose and Pi in ER lumen of the listed glucose-releasing cells.
Verified Cost from pyruvate fact against PDF page image(s) 45: Two pyruvates require 4 ATP, 2 GTP and 2 NADH to form one glucose.
Verified Product feedback fact against PDF page image(s) 51: Glucose 6-phosphate inhibits I–III but does not inhibit liver glucokinase (IV).
Verified Glucose response fact against PDF page image(s) 52: Hexokinase I saturates at low glucose; glucokinase responds across a higher glucose range.
Verified Sequestration fact against PDF page image(s) 53: Regulatory protein retains glucokinase in the nucleus; glucose promotes dissociation.
Verified Energy charge fact against PDF page image(s) 54, 56: ATP inhibits PFK-1; AMP and ADP relieve that inhibition. AMP inhibits FBPase-1.
Verified Citrate fact against PDF page image(s) 55: High citrate increases ATP inhibition of PFK-1, signaling that oxidative fuels meet energy needs.
Verified F26BP fact against PDF page image(s) 57: Increases PFK-1 substrate affinity and lowers FBPase-1 substrate affinity, favoring glycolysis.
Verified Enzyme roles fact against PDF page image(s) 58: PFK-2 forms F26BP; FBPase-2 breaks it down.
Verified Glucagon fact against PDF page image(s) 58: Promotes cAMP-dependent phosphorylation: PFK-2 inactive, FBPase-2 active; F26BP falls.
Verified Insulin fact against PDF page image(s) 58: Promotes dephosphorylation: PFK-2 active, FBPase-2 inactive; F26BP rises and glycolysis is favored.
Verified Feed-forward activation fact against PDF page image(s) 59: Fructose 1,6-bisphosphate activates pyruvate kinase; ATP, acetyl-CoA, long-chain fatty acids and alanine inhibit.
Verified Liver phosphorylation fact against PDF page image(s) 59: Glucagon stimulates PKA-mediated phosphorylation, inactivating pyruvate kinase L.
Verified Acetyl-CoA switch fact against PDF page image(s) 60: Acetyl-CoA activates pyruvate carboxylase and inhibits pyruvate dehydrogenase.

Verified Distribution and substrates fact against PDF page image(s) 14: Hexokinase is found in most tissues and accepts glucose, fructose and mannose; glucokinase is mainly liver/pancreatic β-cells and primarily accepts glucose. Selected p14 table scope; no disputed exact Km.

Rechecked PDF p14 Vmax row after browser QA. Glucokinase has a high Vmax suited to large glucose loads after meals. Hexokinase has a lower Vmax and saturates quickly. No table-column framing or disputed exact Km is used.
